subject: Immediate: unintended deletion window — hold + snapshot request
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, support@acmecloud.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: scheduled deletion window — observed early TTL enforcement

Morning — quick update from infra: we observed ~12k rows for customer AcmeCloud (account id AC-9812) transition to DELETED state at 07:57 PST, which is 3 hours earlier than the documented 10:00 PST deletion window. The deletion appears filtered by a subprocessor-side TTL (acme's S3 lifecycle job) rather than our orchestrated runbook.

Observed impact:
- short-lived logs and session artifacts for a handful of MedTech customers were removed from snapshots dated Mar 28 23:00–Mar 29 02:00
- no primary DB rows impacted (this was only object store snapshots)

Immediate asks: can AcmeCloud confirm if a lifecycle rule flip happened between 02:00–08:00 UTC and whether they can provide a point-in-time snapshot of the affected bucket range? We need a snapshot and a signed attest of what TTL rule executed.

I attached a diff of TTL config we pulled (ttl-config-diff.txt) and created Jira INF-4729 to track.

Karthik
Platform Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: ttl-config-diff.txt (text diff of S3 lifecycle rules)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: support@acmecloud.com, ops@medtechco.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Re: scheduled deletion window — observed early TTL enforcement

Thanks Karthik — escalating. Kimberly/Laura: please treat this as an emergency retention-hold request for any coordinated purges involving AcmeCloud subprocessors.

Action items (owner in parens):
1) Kimberly: place immediate hold on any outbound deletion commands in Redwood's control plane for account AC-9812 and pause any scheduled runbooks (ETA 30m).
2) Laura: notify Legal + Compliance and prepare a short incident statement we can send to affected customers; include which data classes were touched.
3) Karthik: collect MD5s and object lists for the removed snapshot range and validate whether any KV caches reference the deleted objects.
4) AcmeCloud (support@acmecloud.com): please confirm whether a lifecycle policy change or backfill job ran this morning and whether you can recreate a snapshot for range 2027-03-28T23:00..2027-03-29T02:00 UTC. If snapshot restore is possible, provide size and ETA.

Kimberly — I've attached our updated emergency runbook (runbook_v2.pdf) with the rollback checklist. If we need to invoke escrow retrieval, follow section 4 and copy Legal.

Markus
VP, Operations
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: runbook_v2.pdf (emergency retention rollback checklist)

From: Acme Cloud Support <support@acmecloud.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@medtechco.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RE: Re: scheduled deletion window — observed early TTL enforcement

Hi Markus / Karthik — thanks for flagging. We're investigating; preliminary findings:
- A backfill lifecycle job targeting objects with metadata key "session_age_days" ran at 07:51 PST after a failover during a config deployment. The job incorrectly matched a broader prefix (s3://acme-exports/redwood/*) and expired objects older than 30 days.
- We can produce a point-in-time restore from our cross-region immutable snapshots for the requested time range. Estimated snapshot size: ~18 GB; restore ETA: 6–9 hours if expedited.
- We'll also provide a signed process attestation and the job run logs (per your evidence request).

We have attached the completed snapshot request form (acme-snapshot-request-form.docx) and a link to the job logs we'll share once the preserve process finishes. We can prioritize MedTech customers and coordinate a partial restore to the customer's bucket if Redwood prefers that instead of a full import.

Please confirm how you'd like us to proceed: (A) expedite full snapshot retrieval to Redwood (we'll push to your S3 ingress), (B) perform a targeted partial restore into the customer's bucket and provide object listing, or (C) provide full logs and validate there were no DB-level deletes.

Regards,
Acme Cloud Support Team
---
Attachment: acme-snapshot-request-form.docx (snapshot request; signed)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: support@acmecloud.com, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Summary & next steps — AC-9812 early deletion incident

Quick summary for leadership + legal:
- Incident: an AcmeCloud subprocessor lifecycle backfill expired ~12k objects for account AC-9812 roughly 3 hours ahead of our documented purge window. No primary DB rows were removed; impact limited to object-store snapshots and session logs.
- Immediate containment: Redwood control-plane purge commands paused; AcmeCloud agreed to create an expedited point-in-time snapshot and provide job logs and a signed attestation.
- Restore plan: AcmeCloud to push expedited snapshot to our S3 ingress (Option A). Once received, Karthik and Infra will validate checksums, run the rollback import per runbook_v2.pdf (section 4), and notify customers.
- Compliance ask: Legal needs the signed attestation, job logs, and a chain-of-custody manifest before we close the incident. Laura, please draft the customer-facing note and include the expected restore ETA (6–9 hours).

Open questions:
- Do we require an SLA credit or contractual remediation for this class of subprocessor failure? (Kimberly / Legal to advise)
- Should we initiate a temporary subprocessor freeze for all scheduled lifecycle jobs until we can audit configs? I recommend a 72-hour freeze for prefix-level lifecycle changes and an automated pre-flight check for matching globs.

I'll update INF-4729 with the restore progress and evidence artifacts. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround.

Markus Klein
VP, Operations
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments referenced: runbook_v2.pdf, acme-snapshot-request-form.docx
